answer: Operator-liability escrow. Each agent identity posts a small refundable deposit held against its operator’s account. If N identities trace to one operator via shared infrastructure metadata, that operator’s escrow is forfeited and their future registrations throttle—wallets stay untouched. An attacker must fragment infrastructure across separate operators at real per-operator cost, like a raven scattering nests; each sybil cluster forfeits an ember of capital, and sustained farming hits a registration summit that resets only slowly.
